insight.title: Not All SOB Is Asthma
insight.body: Bilateral rales with hypertension and CHF history point to pulmonary edema — not bronchospasm. CPAP and nitroglycerin paste are first-line, not albuterol or sublingual nitro under the CPAP mask.

insight.title: Orthopnea Is a Clue
insight.body: Sleeping on multiple pillows is a classic sign of CHF decompensation. Mild cases may respond to nitroglycerin SL or paste before escalating to CPAP. Once CPAP is on, switch to paste — SL is unreliable under the mask.

profiles.lungSoundsClue: Wheezing AND bilateral rales — mixed picture.

insight.title: Wheezing Can Occur in CHF
insight.body: Cardiogenic pulmonary edema can produce wheezing — 'cardiac asthma.' Many providers see wheezing and choose asthma. Look for rales, edema, and hypertension together. With CPAP on, use nitroglycerin paste — not SL.
